extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, event organizers, and anyone writing press releases for events
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and timing event press releases that generate media coverage and attendance, including structure (headline, lead, body, boilerplate), targeting, tone, and variants by event type and timeline stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong headline and dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: An event press release needs a strong headline and dateline to lead the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should grab attention and highlight the most newsworthy angle (e.g., product reveal, high-profile speaker). Dateline establishes timing/location. Use concise, specific language rather than vague hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph with the five Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead paragraph should sum up the five Ws: who, what, when, where and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the essential information up front so journalists can quickly understand the event. This is your primary news hook — make it clear and factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting details, quotes and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the body to expand on the lead with supporting details, relevant data, and quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotes from organizers, speakers or experts to add personality and credibility. Use data or statistics to back claims about impact or importance. Organize supporting facts so they follow logically from the lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: End with clear call to action, boilerplate, and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude with a strong, clear call to action, an up-to-date company press release boilerplate, and media contact info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell readers what you want them to do (buy tickets, register, attend). Ensure the boilerplate succinctly describes the organization and is current. Provide a named contact with phone/email for media follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify an angle / newsworthiness (hook)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find an angle that makes the audience care and makes the event newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask what makes the event special — first-of-its-kind, keynote speaker with large following, charitable component, or a major product reveal. Use that angle to craft a compelling headline and lead that will make journalists pay attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target the right journalists and outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Send the press release to journalists and outlets that cover events like yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research reporters and outlets that have covered similar events, build a targeted media list (e.g., financial reporters for business conferences, entertainment writers for music festivals, environmental reporters for sustainability summits). Use distribution services where appropriate to reach the correct beats and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fluff and slang; use concrete details
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use hype words or slang; instead use concrete details and supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases like “game-changing” or “revolutionize the industry” are fluff without evidence. Provide specifics, numbers, and context that demonstrate importance rather than hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all key logistical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for journalists and attendees by including date, time, location, ticket info and other logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also mention special guests, unique features, charitable components, celebrity appearances, or record attempts — these details can turn a listing into a feature. Journalists are busy; upfront logistics reduce friction for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor press release to event type: product launches
rubrics_metrics.description: Product launch event releases should emphasize what’s new and innovative about the product and how it solves problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight benefits, real-world applications, and include quotes from experts, influencers or customers to add credibility and excitement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor press release to event type: partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnership event releases should showcase how organizations are combining strengths and the benefits of the collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the unique value created by the partnership and mention any charitable causes or social impact tied to the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor press release to event type: educational events
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational event releases should emphasize learning opportunities and expert insights attendees will gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what makes the event unique as an educational opportunity, list learning outcomes or session highlights, and include a clear sign-up or registration link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor press release to event type: retail and sales events
rubrics_metrics.description: Retail/sales event releases should highlight special deals, limited-time offers or exclusive products and the value to shoppers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear about discounts, eligibility, and any philanthropic tie-ins. Make the value proposition and urgency obvious to drive attendance/sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor press release to event type: concerts and festivals
rubrics_metrics.description: Concert/festival releases should generate buzz by emphasizing star power, unique venue features, and special experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on big-name performers, exclusive experiences, and create a sense of FOMO (fear of missing out) to drive ticket sales and media interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce the event (initial release)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the initial announcement release to present the big picture: what the event is, why it matters, when and where it’s happening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send once the event is confirmed; include a quote from an organizer or key participant to add personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce the agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: When the schedule is set, send an agenda-focused release highlighting key sessions and how the agenda supports event goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: send a few weeks before the event to help media and attendees plan coverage. Emphasize sessions that are most newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce the speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue a speakers release to highlight keynotes and notable presenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include each speaker’s title and organization; for major speakers, add a detailed bio and quotes about why they’re participating. If many speakers are involved, a list may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update during the event / real-time releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue breaking-news releases during the event for notable occurrences (award winners, surprise announcements, competition results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-time updates can attract live media coverage and social buzz. Be ready to distribute short, timely releases with the news and supporting context as events unfold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recap each day for multi-day events
rubrics_metrics.description: Send daily recaps summarizing key moments, quotes and previews of upcoming sessions for multi-day events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recaps keep momentum and remote audiences engaged; include standout quotes and highlights to sustain media interest across days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap up / post-event press release
rubrics_metrics.description: After the event, send a comprehensive summary within a day or two that highlights attendance numbers, famous attendees and memorable moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key metrics, major outcomes, notable quotes, and what made the event successful. Promptly issuing a wrap-up helps secure end-of-event coverage and sets up next-year promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce the next event
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize on momentum by announcing follow-up or next-year dates and early details while excitement is high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the next event date and any early details to keep audiences and media engaged and to start building anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length, formatting and scannability
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep releases concise and scannable: generally 300–800 words, with essential information in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short paragraphs and bullet points for easy scanning. Longer releases are acceptable for large speaker lists or multi-day recaps, but always prioritize the lead and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-event release content specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-event releases should include summaries of highlights, attendance numbers, key outcomes, and quotes from organizers/participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also mention records set or major announcements made, and include a note about the next event if applicable. These specifics help editors convert recaps into feature stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and targeting: send right people at the right time
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing distribution matters: send releases to the appropriate audience segments and at stages aligned with newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted distribution lists and consider distribution services to reach thousands of journalists or niche beats. Match the release stage (announcement, agenda, speaker, live update, recap) to journalists’ planning and publishing cycles.
